script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

MRS. NORA JAMES (40s) sits on an oversized couch, a stack of papers in her lap. Her husband JASON (40s) enters, looking tired and worn.

JASON
(sighs)
You're still at it?

NORA
(exasperated)
I can't keep ignoring it, Jason. This is our lives we're talking about.

Jason slumps into the recliner, rubbing his eyes.

JASON
I know, sweetheart, but what can we do? We've tried everything.

Nora looks down at her papers, her expression turning serious.

NORA
I think I might have an idea. But it's going to take all of us.

EXT. JAMES HOME - DAY

Nora, Jason, and their three kids, JESSICA (15), MIKE (12), and SAM (8), sit in the backyard, surrounded by an array of art supplies.

NORA
(passionate)
I propose we start our own family business. Something that not only brings us closer together but also helps us find our identities.

JESSICA
(skeptical)
A family business? Like what?

NORA
(smiling)
I thought you'd never ask. I want us to start a small artisanal bakery. We can all contribute our unique talents.

MIKE
(excited)
Yeah! I can help with the baking.

SAM
(eager)
And I can decorate the cakes!

JASON
(amused)
And I'll handle the finances.

NORA
(proud)
That's the spirit.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

The family works together, baking and decorating cakes for their first sale the following day.

NORA
(whispering to Jason)
I'm so glad we did this, Jason.

JASON
(smiling)
Me too.

EXT. FARMERS MARKET - DAY

The family sets up their stall, proudly displaying their creations. Customers begin to gather, and the family works together to make sales.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Nora, Jason, and their kids sit on the couch, exhausted but content.

JASON
(smiling)
Today was a success. I can't believe how well we all worked together.

NORA
(satisfied)
I knew we could do it. We found our identity as a family, and I'm so proud of us.

JESSICA
(grateful)
Thanks, Mom. I really enjoy being a part of this.

MIKE
(agreed)
Me too. It's fun and we get to make people happy.

SAM
(excitedly)
Can we do it again tomorrow?

NORA
(laughs)
Absolutely, Sam. We'll do it every day.

The family hugs, their eyes shining with love and unity.

FADE OUT.
